question.text: Aravalli Long-Short Fund (Cat III open-ended) has used Valuer X for the last three years for its unlisted-equity positions. Per SEBI's valuation framework amendments, what is the MOST APPROPRIATE next step regarding valuer appointments?

answer.text: Continue Valuer X indefinitely since results have been consistent

Rotate to a new independent valuer on the prescribed rotation cadence and ensure the new entity meets the APMI empanelment and IBBI/Section 247 Registered Valuer Entity eligibility per the September 2024 SEBI Circular
Appoint the fund's auditor as the valuer to save costs
Dispense with external valuation since Valuer X has a long history

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Regulation 23 and the September 19, 2024 SEBI Circular, the independent valuer must be IBBI-registered (individual) or a Registered Valuer Entity with ICAI/ICSI/ICMAI/CFA-charter authorised persons, and cannot be an associate. Rotation at the prescribed cadence ensures independence. Long-tenure continuation undermines the independence principle; appointing the auditor violates independence; dispensing with external valuation breaches Reg 23. The Trap: A, C, D all violate independence rules. Continuity > compliance is not a defensible position. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C and XIX-D test rotation/eligibility. Sep-2024 amendment applies across all AIF categories. Manager's Pro-Tip: Maintain a standing panel of 3 pre-vetted APMI-empanelled RVEs - when rotation is due, switching is 2 weeks not 2 months. Include an MOU for data-access so the new valuer doesn't start cold.
